import time
from functools import wraps

TTL = 60  # seconds; tune to how stale a profile may be

_cache = {}  # ponytail: in-process dict, no eviction. Swap for Redis if you run >1 instance or memory grows.

def cached_profile(fn):
    @wraps(fn)
    def wrapper(user_id):
        hit = _cache.get(user_id)
        if hit and time.monotonic() - hit[0] < TTL:
            return hit[1]
        value = fn(user_id)
        _cache[user_id] = (time.monotonic(), value)
        return value
    return wrapper

def invalidate_profile(user_id):
    _cache.pop(user_id, None)


# --- usage ---
@cached_profile
def get_profile(user_id):
    return api.fetch_profile(user_id)   # your existing call

def update_profile(user_id, data):
    api.update_profile(user_id, data)
    invalidate_profile(user_id)         # don't serve stale data after a write

        return {"id": uid}
    fake(1); fake(1)
    assert calls == [1], "second call should hit cache"
    invalidate_profile(1); fake(1)
    assert calls == [1, 1], "invalidate should force refetch"
    _cache[2] = (time.monotonic() - TTL - 1, {"id": 2}); fake(2)
    assert calls == [1, 1, 2], "expired entry should refetch"
